question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{{6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{(x-2)^{4}(3-x)^{3}}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient, product, and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{(x-2)^{4}(3-x)^{3}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})-\operatorname{ln}⁡((x-2)^{4}(3-x)^{3}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡6-(\operatorname{ln}⁡((x-2)^{4})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((3-x)^{3})) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡6-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡6)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡6)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4\cdot \frac{1}{x-2}-3\cdot \frac{-1}{3-x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-(\operatorname{ln}⁡6)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{4}{x-2}+\frac{3}{3-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(-(\operatorname{ln}⁡6)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{4}{x-2}+\frac{3}{3-x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{{6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{(x-2)^{4}(3-x)^{3}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{{6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{(x-2)^{4}(3-x)^{3}}(-(\operatorname{ln}⁡6)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{4}{x-2}+\frac{3}{3-x}) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{(x-2)^{4}(3-x)^{3}}(\frac{-(\operatorname{ln}⁡6)(x-2)(3-x)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4(3-x)+3(x-2)}{(x-2)(3-x)}) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{(x-2)^{4}(3-x)^{3}}(\frac{-(\operatorname{ln}⁡6)(x-2)(3-x)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7x-18}{(x-2)(3-x)}) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡6(x-2)(3-x)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7x-18)}{(x-2)^{5}(3-x)^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$
